title: Dame
brief_context: Mentioned regarding her interest in women in Middle East.
brief_extract: In her article Miss George mentioned that the Caroline Haslett Memorial Trust had been asked to consider the award of an exhibition to one of the Arab women staff at the centre to enable her to spend some months studying technical training methods in this country. This proposal commended itself to the Trust particularly in view of the interest Dame Caroline Haslett had taken in the role of women in the Middle East and also because nearly half of the cost of building and equipping the centre had been met by the United Kingdom World Refugee Fund. An exhibition was accordingly offered through the United Nations Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA) and the selected recipient is Miss Nada Sfeir who is the Domestic Bursar at the centre.

brief_extract:
FINDING A HOME

MARY GEORGE, MBE, Director EAW,
describes an interesting housing project of the Over 40
Association for Women, of which she is Chairman

A corner of the electric kitchen

THIRTY years ago at the time of the econom-
ic depression the plight of many single
women was piteous, older women who lost
their jobs had little hopes of finding new ones,
and even women who were only 30 or 40 were
regarded as too old by employers. It was to help
such women in their difficulties that the Over
Thirty Association was founded in London.

brief_extract: Although china is manufactured by other countries, bone china is made exclusively in England. The process was perfected by Josiah Spode about 1805 and since then English bone china has become world famous. The cost of china has altered considerably in recent years; once bone china was considered very expensive and although this still applies if an intricate design using gold and expensive colourings is required, a tea service can be purchased for as little as £4.

brief_context: Hypothetical recipient of a model train set.
brief_extract:
Electric toys
Looking gift horses in the mouth is not usually a commendable activity, but it can be at Christmas time, if the gift is electrical. If it's a model train set for young George, for example, it may be designed to run from the mains through what is called an auto-transformer. This differs from the completely safe type of transformer in that it doesn't have two entirely separate and distinct windings; it is therefore quite possible for the mains voltage to reach the model train and its rails if any kind of earth return path is available, such as a water pipe, water-filled radiator or a concrete floor.

D. Pegrum, Magazine Secretary, Dursley

Standing on the River Severn between Gloucester and 
Bristol, the modern buildings of Berkeley Power Station 
provide a fascinating contrast with historical Berkeley 
Castle, scene of the murder of Edward II, only a mile 
away. Work at Berkeley was started in 1957 and the station 
began feeding into the National Grid in June 1962.

title: HRH; Duke
brief_context: Performed the official opening of the Berkeley power station.
article_title: VISIT TO BERKELEY NUCLEAR POWER STATION
brief_extract:
Work at Berkeley was started in 1957 and the station 
began feeding into the National Grid in June 1962. The 
official opening by HRH the Duke of Edinburgh was 
performed jointly with the 'twin' station at Bradwell in 
Essex in April 1963. With an installed capacity of 322 mw and an output of
275 mw Berkeley is the smallest of nine nuclear stations in 
the present CEGB programme.
